evidence.excerpt: University HPC clusters frequently host both long-running genomic assembly jobs and short, interactive variant-calling tasks submitted by clinical collaborators. We ran a six-month measurement study on a 640-core cluster at the University of Novi Sad, logging 18 400 job submissions across three user groups. We then replayed the trace under five SLURM scheduling configurations—backfill-only, priority preemption, gang scheduling, fair-share with decay factor 0.5, and a hybrid policy—using a discrete-event simulator we built in Python. The hybrid policy combining fair-share weighting with selective preemption of low-priority assembly jobs reduced median wait time for clinical variant-calling tasks from 47 minutes to 11 minutes, at the cost of a 3 % increase in total cluster makespan over the trace period. We describe configuration parameters, discuss trade-offs for clusters with heterogeneous node types, and release the simulator and anonymised job trace under an open licence.
